summary: Recent testimony of an old observation. Observation of the silent movement of a black "tube" with three red colour zones (two at the ends and one in the centre): lack of information.
description: Recent report (2008) of an earlier sighting. On Saturday, November 2, 1974, around 8:30 p.m., a driver and his passenger were startled by the slow, silent movement of a tube-shaped object, black with three very dark red areas: two at the ends and one in the middle. The witness got out of his vehicle and saw the object rise vertically, then move very slowly over the road and the trees before disappearing. The sighting lasted several minutes before the frightened witnesses resumed their journey. Only one report has been collected about this phenomenon. This 1974 sighting was not reported to GEIPAN until 2008, and consequently, it was given low priority. This nocturnal observation of a "velvet-black" tube bordered by three luminous discs must first be analyzed using the tools of perceptual psychology (the so-called contour or shape illusion): it is very common for an observer of a set of luminous points moving together to mentally reconstruct a volume bounded by these points. In this case, while the presence of the three luminous discs (called portholes by the witness) is beyond doubt, the existence of the tube should not be considered certain. Therefore, the phenomenon becomes a set of three luminous discs moving slowly together, which could correspond to luminous objects carried by the wind, such as Thai lanterns, very common nowadays (2016), but very rare in France at that time. It should be noted that the observation took place on a Saturday evening at 8:30 p.m., a time conducive to festive events. It is also All Souls' Day. Some people symbolically honor their deceased by licking Thai lanterns. While this hypothesis is plausible, GEIPAN cannot confirm it, firstly because there is no weather report to correlate the movement of the lights with local winds, and secondly because Thai lanterns were used at the time only by Asians or tourists returning from Thailand. Unable to verify this information or find other corroborating evidence, GEIPAN classifies this case as Category C due to lack of information.

summary: observation of a ball in the sky.
description: On October 10, 1974, at 5:55 PM, a school supervisor was alerted by students to a peculiar phenomenon in the sky. Going outside the school, the witness spotted a silvery sphere and two other smaller spheres. These appeared to be connected to the larger sphere by a thread. The witness decided to alert her husband and lost sight of the whole thing. The next day, she was told that the two smaller spheres had risen inside the larger one before speeding off again. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack data.

summary: Observation of three bright points in the sky.
description: Recent testimony (May 14, 2008) of a past observation. In May or June 1974 or 1975, a witness observed, from their 5th-floor apartment, three fixed points of light at an altitude of approximately 200 to 300 meters. After several minutes and without any noise, these points of light approached the cele and then moved away to the south. No other testimonies or further details have been collected regarding this phenomenon.
